title: China Accuses the US of Dividing Mexico over Trade Dispute
author: José Shaddai Olvera Torres
content:
_This article by[José Shaddai Olvera
Torres](https://elchamuco.com.mx/author/shaddai/) originally appeared in the
[September 18, 2026 edition of El Chamuco y los Hijos del
Averno](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/09/18/china-critica-eu-mexico-made-in-
china/), a Mexican satirical and political magazine._

The Embassy of China in Mexico accused the US diplomatic mission of attempting
to generate divisions between the two countries through a message spread
during the celebrations of Mexican Independence.

The protest arose from a message published on **September 15** by the US
Embassy with the phrase **" Viva México, Made in China,"** referring to the
foreign origin of the fireworks and other products used during the patriotic
festivities.

In a **" Solemn Declaration,"** the Chinese mission held that the message
ignored elementary norms of diplomatic courtesy and disrespected the Mexican
people.

> [Post by @USEmbassyMEX on
> X](https://twitter.com/USEmbassyMEX/status/2099996686223397006)

The Embassy also reproached the United States for taking advantage of one of
Mexico's main national dates to question a third nation, instead of sending
congratulations.

## China Defends Its Trade Relationship With Mexico

The Chinese mission maintained that it is up to the Mexican people to decide
how to celebrate their Independence and which countries to choose as trading
partners.

> A nation's Independence Day belongs to its people. How and with what to
> celebrate it is decided by its own people.
>
> Embassy of China in Mexico

![Cartoon on the US-China dispute over
Mexico](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/02-china-
cartoon.jpg)Illustration: Fer / El Chamuco

Beijing also defended Mexico's right, as an independent state, to freely
establish its commercial relations.

The Embassy recalled that exchanges between Mexico and China have a history of
more than four centuries, linked to the **Nao de China** (the Manila Galleon),
when Asian products such as silk and porcelain were exchanged for Mexican
silver.

According to the Chinese position, that historical relationship represents a
process of exchange and learning between the two societies.

## Beijing Accuses Washington of Using the Mexican Celebration

The Chinese Embassy held that the US publication turned the Mexican national
celebration into a stage for the geopolitical dispute between Washington and
Beijing.

In its declaration, it described the US comments as an expression of **"
supremacy and hegemony"** and asserted that they sought to discredit the
economic cooperation between Mexico and China.

Finally, the Chinese mission asked its US counterpart to respect the host
country and to focus on strengthening the ties between the two peoples.

It also questioned what it described as an attempt to **" sow discord and
division,"** and held that this strategy would end up harming those who
promote it.

The controversy occurs in a context of tension over the commercial and
geopolitical relations among the **United States, Mexico, and China** , with
Washington recurrently questioning the presence of Chinese products and
investments in Mexican territory.
